stumbles.quote: 42/43 violations with any directive or none
stumbles.why: Unclear what the violations are (violations of what rule/task?), what 43 refers to (trials?), and what 'any directive or none' means without the experimental setup.

stumbles.quote: Every directive naming a forbidden word raised its log-odds ~2.5.
stumbles.why: Unclear whose log-odds: the forbidden word's probability of being produced? It also seems to conflict with 'changed nothing' since violations were already 42/43 and caps vs. not isn't separated from naming.
It's not stated what was compared (caps vs. lowercase directives), and 'directive' is undefined, so the claim is hard to interpret.

stumbles.quote: Its 22,100 training docs hold one caps rule: 'NEVER give a baby honey'.
stumbles.why: It's not explained how the training corpus is known or why that matters; the implied link (caps are nearly absent from training data so the model can't use them) is left unsaid. 'Its' also has a distant referent.
Unexplained model name; the reader must guess it's a small language model with 321M parameters.

point: In a tiny 321M-parameter model, capitalized emphasis didn't reduce rule violations, and naming a forbidden word in any instruction made it more likely to appear, perhaps because its training data has almost no caps-style rules.
